body: To fix it in webpack, we would need to get the timestamps when calling invalidate, but this requires a change of the WatchFileSystem interface. So this would be a breaking change. We can do that for webpack 4.
Why would it have to be a breaking change; could it not be additive?

This would likely be an improvement for most people, plus vs. a new config
option+opt in, this makes sense to me.

@sokra the workeraround looks nice.
We've also hit by this issue at Next.js.

As a workaround we `touch` a file when starting the app. Then it invalidates first.
And it introduce many other issues.

Looking forward for a proper fix. 
But again the workaround looks cleaner than what we have now.

> Why would it have to be a breaking change; could it not be additive?

The WatchFileSystem has no interface method to `getTimes`. We can add this method to the NodeWatchFileSystem, but if somebody provided a custom watch filesystem this will be broken. So it's a breaking change, but I guess only 1-3 people provided a custom watch filesystem and need to change their code.

Anyway webpack 4 is in the pipeline. We can add it there.

I'm totally fine with waiting until webpack 4 for this. We've implemented
the workaround in our server, waiting for more data to see the impact, but
I expect to see some significant dev performance boosts.

body: @sokra Just a quick update here. We've been working on getting on webpack 4 and I tried removing our workaround for this and the problem seems to still be there. For now we'll just keep our workaround, but it would be nice if this just worked without it.

I just hit on this issue as well, because I was trying to figure out why the `compilation.fileTimestamps` is always empty on first compile.

I would say that this bug has definitely not been fixed. Too bad, as it makes it really hard to check for changed source files etc. (Really biting me with service workers where they install/activate for any change which this bug is causing)

issue.title: Make the plugin play nice with webpack dev middleware

repository.name: serviceworker-webpack-plugin
repository.description: Simplifies creation of a service worker to serve your webpack bundles. :recycle:

issue.body:
Hi there, this plugin has been very useful for us as we start integrating service workers into our apps. Thanks!

The one thing that was driving me nuts was that when running webpack in dev mode (with webpack dev middleware), the service worker was getting re-generated on every change to any file. (which then triggers the browser to go and install it)

The main reason for this constant regeneration is that in dev mode, webpack only emits the assets that have changed, which was causing the service worker manifest to "lose files" and be recompiled each time. (so on every change the service worker would break! :-( )

This PR fixes that issue by switching the plugin to additively add assets to the manifest as they come in. It only happens when compiler.watchMode === true, so production environments should be unaffected by this change.

Once I fixed the manifest issue, I needed to figure out how to still detect changes to the service worker code itself. To that end, I was going to use the timestamps, but there's a bug in webpack (https://github.com/webpack/webpack/issues/5970) So I ended up using webpack's internal file system to diff the service worker source files manually.

Not the cleanest solution, but it's working super reliably for me!

I'd be willing to look at adding some actual tests for this, but I'm unfamiliar with how to test webpack in a dev kind of setup... :-/
